title: After Wooing Trump With Deals, Pakistan Gets a Seat at the Table
partialText: Steve Witkoff, a diplomatic envoy, used the Board of Peace to announce an agreement that could raze a Pakistan-owned Manhattan hotel. Now the country is involved in negotiating peace talks with Iran.

title: Europe Heads for Another Energy Shock as Iran War Raises Natural Gas Prices
partialText: The region’s stores of natural gas are running at the lowest level in years, and filling them up is increasingly daunting as the U.S.-led war in Iran pushes up prices.

title: Juries Take the Lead in the Push for Child Online Safety
partialText: A pair of verdicts held social media companies accountable for harming young users, highlighting a growing backlash as Congress struggles to pass legislation.

title: Is Big Tech Facing a Big Tobacco Moment?
partialText: Back-to-back courtroom losses have put technology giants, including Meta and Google, in uncertain territory as they face lawsuits and bans on teen users.

title: The Social Media Addiction Trials: What to Know
partialText: Landmark trials are testing a new legal strategy claiming that Meta, TikTok, Snap and YouTube caused personal injury through addictive products.

title: Some Judges See Risks in Fiery Opinions Warning of Threats to Democracy
partialText: Federal judges are weighing strategies for how to respond to the high stakes, anonymous threats and politicized atmosphere of the Trump era.

title: Trump Calls for Law Cracking Down on Crime and ‘Rogue Judges’
partialText: Ahead of the midterms, President Trump told a Republican gathering that he wants to go after repeat offenders and “rogue judges that are criminals.”

title: ‘Lethality’ Used to Be a Pentagon Buzzword. Now It’s a Worldview.
partialText: It’s blunt instead of vague, brash instead of evasive, bold instead of cautious. And yet the word obfuscates as much as old defense jargon.

title: Olympic Committee Bars Transgender Athletes From Women’s Events
partialText: The decision is the most significant since Kirsty Coventry was elected last year to serve as president of the I.O.C.

title: When a Not-So-Dark Knight and His Sidekick Saved a Wacky Gotham
partialText: Joel Schumacher apologized for “Batman & Robin,” his corny 1997 superhero movie, but thanks to its ice puns and bat nipples, it’s since become an accidental parody worth howling at.

title: ICE Agents at Some Airports Begin Checking IDs in Security Lines
partialText: It was unclear whether having agents helping with screening passengers would improve wait times. Some travelers expressed worries.

title: LaGuardia Airport Runway Reopens After Plane Crash Wreckage Is Removed
partialText: Officials expect the airport in New York to be fully operational later on Thursday. One of its two runways had been closed since Sunday, when a jet hit a truck, killing two pilots.

title: In California’s Central Valley, Latino Voters are Up for Grabs in 2026’s Elections
partialText: As in other Hispanic areas of the country, voters shifted toward Republicans in 2024. But there are increasing signs that this was a blip more than a durable trend.

title: Wealthy Investors Target Foes of Clean Energy, Seeking Revenge
partialText: Renewable energy leaders said their industry got “rolled” in President Trump’s tax bill. Now they’re fighting back, starting in Texas.

title: South Dakota Governor Signs Bill Requiring Citizenship Proof to Vote
partialText: The law, which mirrors national Republican priorities, requires newly registered voters to show that they are U.S. citizens in order to cast a ballot in state or local races.

title: Savannah Guthrie Says 2 Ransom Notes About Her Mother Were Likely Genuine
partialText: Her interview on the “Today” show came more than 50 days after her mother, Nancy Guthrie, was taken from her home near Tucson, Ariz.

title: Binance Under Fire After Reports That $1.7 Billion in Crypto Flowed to Iran
partialText: The world’s largest crypto exchange is under fire after investigators found accounts moving $1.7 billion to Iranian entities. Clues about those accounts were in plain sight for over a year.

title: Saving Hermit Crabs by Breeding Them in the Suburbs
partialText: Often treated as throwaway pets, hermit crabs can live 50 years. Mary Akers, a self-taught expert, wants people to appreciate them as much as she does.

title: Colleges Pressed to Remove Names of Epstein’s Friends From Buildings
partialText: Students and others are asking universities, including Harvard and Ohio State, to take down the names of high-profile donors with connections to Jeffrey Epstein. They have not done so yet.

title: Zelensky Says U.S. Is Conditioning Ukraine’s Security Guarantees on Donbas Surrender
partialText: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said that President Trump “still chooses a strategy of putting more pressure on the Ukrainian side.”

title: In Rural Ukraine, Basic Health Care Is a Casualty of War
partialText: Elderly people in isolated villages are going without medicine. One woman said she hadn’t seen a doctor in four years.

title: Russian Lawmakers Go to U.S. for First Time Since Invasion of Ukraine
partialText: The State Department had to lift sanctions on Russian lawmakers invited by a Kremlin-friendly member of Congress.

title: Under Carney, Canada Finally Hits NATO’s 2% Spending Target
partialText: Trump and other American presidents have criticized Canada for failing to meet the alliance’s military spending minimum of 2 percent of gross domestic product.

title: The Sudden Death of a Man Who Told Chinese Kids How to Succeed
partialText: The influencer Zhang Xuefeng was known for no-nonsense, some said cynical, advice about how to win in China’s educational rat race. He died at 41.

title: The Strait of Hormuz Closed Because Iran Is Using the U.S. Playbook
partialText: Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz by raising risks for ship operators. In doing so, it has taken lessons from American financial policy.

title: It’s Not Trump. It’s America.
partialText: The country’s faith in its ability to shape the world to its liking is a much older malady.

title: The Kennedy Center Is Giving Bill Maher the Mark Twain Prize
partialText: The annual award that recognizes merit in humor is going to the satirist and talk show host who has been critical of President Trump and political correctness.

title: Immigration Slowdown Hits Every Metro Area in the U.S., Census Shows
partialText: Large urban counties and the border were the most affected. And in three-quarters of U.S. counties, population growth either slowed or turned negative.

title: Cuban Patients Are Dying Because of U.S. Blockade, Doctors Say
partialText: Cuban health care was once the pride of the island. Now the U.S. oil blockade is upending even basic medical care.

title: Mamdani Promised to Freeze the Rent. Now the Fight Begins.
partialText: Nine board members, six of whom were appointed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, will meet Thursday to begin weighing whether to enact a rent freeze.
